doc.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: First records: Ellington and race records
summary: His first records were Ellington's Koko and Truckin', bought before he owned a player; he recalls Ellington's mutes and race records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: My first records were “Koko” by Ellington, “Koko,” “Truckin’” —

No, no, no, no. Ellington wrote a thing called “Koko,” which somebody later stole and used it. They always used things of his though. Like “Night Train” is the fourth tenor part of “Happy Go Lucky” of Ellington’s. But who was it that did [scats] Great line. Then Joe Nanton came in [scats].
Oh you’re marvelous. You’re a whole band.
But those are things I grew up with. I bought those records before I had anything to play on. I couldn’t — I didn’t have a machine. Later on I got a machine to play them on. But I loved the music.
They have the most fantastic use of the mutes, the most creative. Up until that time and never since has it been surpassed.
I used to cover the “Sophisticated Jungle.” Really sophisticated.
Well they called it jungle music.
Oh sure they did. Well they had a name for it all. They had race records. You’d race to the store and get ‘em. Thirty cents. Thirty-five cents. Boy.
